newsitem.title: UK: British biotech firms funded by tobacco - journal.
newsitem.headline: British biotech firms funded by tobacco - journal.

text.p: Funding by tobacco companies of medical research is widespread across Britain, researchers for a medical charity reported on Friday.
Dr Grant Lewison and colleagues at the Wellcome Trust said they found a considerable number of references to studies funded at least in part by tobacco companies.
Last year a vocal row broke out when another charity, the Medical Research Council, said it had taken money from tobacco companies.

"It is evident that the practice of accepting tobacco money was widespread and of the UK's medical schools only Glasgow does not feature," Lewison's group wrote in a letter to the Lancet medical journal.

They examined 185,000 biomedical papers listed in the Wellcome Trust's database from 1988 to 1994. They were looking for funding from major tobacco companies, including the Tobacco Products Research Trust and the Health Promotion Research Trust, a charity set up by tobacco companies in 1983.
"Over the seven years, there were 269 papers acknowledging support from the tobacco industry for tobacco-related research," they wrote. They said this was bad for the image of medical research.
"Not only is smoking tobacco harmful to health but there is a belief that the companies will attempt to silence researchers whose findings are unpalatable," they wrote.

"Consequently there is a suspicion that researchers who accept money from the tobacco industry, whether directly from a company or from a charitable foundation financed by the industry, are compromising their integrity."
The Cancer Research Campaign and other medical charities say they are drawing up a code of practice about such funding.
